paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Nehemiah has a finished wall, shut doors and guards on duty, and a city that is "large and spacious, but there were few people in it" (Nehemiah 7:4). A wall without people is just a very fancy fence. So God puts something into Nehemiah's heart (Nehemiah 7:5): it's time to count the people.

And look at what a list does. Every family gets named, town by town, and nobody is skipped because the number is too big. I spent years in a drawer thinking nobody was keeping count of me, so this hits close to home. Your name matters to God too, and He keeps a better register than any drawer ever did. Even the priests who couldn't find their records weren't brushed aside in a hurry. The governor told them to wait until a priest could consult the Urim and Thummim (Nehemiah 7:64-65).

So here's your takeaway, baker. Building something is only half the job, because God cares about the people who get to live in it. Then they settled in their own towns (Nehemiah 7:73), and that's the picture: a people with a place and a name. Show up, be counted and be part of the people of God. The story isn't over, either, so keep those ovens warm.
